sentences.text: Hello, everyone. Welcome to the Slow English Podcast. My name is Emili. We speak slowly
here. We use easy English. We repeat important ideas. Today, we travel to Africa, but not
to a big city, not to Nairobi. Today, we visit a small and quiet island town. Its name
is Lamu. Lamu is peaceful. Lamu is traditional. Lamu feels different from modern cities. Take
a deep breath. Relax. Let us begin our journey. Where is Lamu? Lamu is in Kenya in East Africa.
It is on the coast of the Indian Ocean. It is not easy to reach. You take a small plane or a boat.
Lamu is an island. There are no cars. Yes, no cars. You walk. You ride a donkey. You use a boat.
Life moves slowly here. Part 3. A town without cars. Lamu has no traffic noise, no car horns,
no busy roads. The streets are very narrow. Some streets are so small that two people walk
carefully. People use donkeys for transport. You see them everywhere.
This makes the town quiet. Very quiet. You hear footsteps. You hear the sea. You hear the wind.
Part 4. Part 4. History of Lamu. Lamu is very old and 700 years old. It was part of the Swahili
Coast culture. Arab traders came here. Indian traders came here. You can see this history in
the buildings. Doors are big and wooden. Walls are white. Houses have inner court yards. History
lives here. Part 5. Swahili culture. Lamu is important for Swahili culture. People speak Swahili.
Religion is important. Traditions are strong. This women wear colorful clothes. Men wear
white robes sometimes. Life feels traditional. People respect old customs. Culture is not a show
here. It is daily life. Part 6. The Ocean and Daily Life. The Indian Ocean is very close.
You smell salt in the air. Boats called dows move slowly. They use wind power.
Fishermen go out early in the morning. They bring fresh fish. The sea gives food. The sea gives
calm. In the evening, people sit near the water. They watch the sunset.
Part 7. Slow daily rhythm. Life starts early in Lamu. The morning is cool. People open small shops.
Children go to school. Afternoon is hot. Very hot. People rest. They sit in the shade. Evening
becomes active again. Neighbors talk. Children laugh. Life follows the sun.
Part 8. Food in Lamu. Food is rich in spices. Rice is common. Fish is fresh.
Coconut is used often. You taste cardamom. You taste cinnamon. Tea is sweet and strong.
Coffee smells deep. Meals are shared. Food brings people together.
Part 9. The Call to Prayer. Religion is part of daily life. You hear the call to prayer.
It echoes through the town. People stop working. They go to the mosque. The sound is soft and
beautiful. It brings peace. Even if you are not religious, you feel calm when you hear it.
Part 10. Festivals and Donkey Race. Lamu has a special festival every year.
There is music. There is poetry. There are boat races. And there is something unique.
A donkey race. Yes, a donkey race. People laugh. People cheer. It is simple joy. The festival
shows community spirit. Part 11. Silence and Reflection. At night, Lamu becomes very quiet.
There are few lights. You see stars clearly. You hear the sea. You hear soft wind. There is space
to think. No rush. No pressure. No noise. Lamu teaches patience. It teaches slow living.
Part 12. The Soul of Lamu and Goodbye. Lamu is not modern. Lamu is not fast. But Lamu is real.
It is simple. It is traditional. It is calm. Life moves with nature. Not against it.
